title: When iterating over an iterable object, using list() should be avoided
description: Converting an iterable to a list using list() constructor when only iteration is needed creates unnecessary memory overhead and reduces performance. Direct iteration over the iterable is more memory-efficient and faster.
message: Avoid using list() when iterating over an iterable; iterate directly instead.
impact: Converting iterables to lists unnecessarily consumes memory and degrades performance, especially with large datasets. This can lead to memory exhaustion and slower execution times.
recommendation: Remove the list() conversion and iterate directly over the iterable object.

references.title: Effective Python - Item 27: Use Comprehensions Instead of map and filter

noncompliant.description: Converting range() to list creates unnecessary memory overhead
Converting a generator to list defeats the purpose of lazy evaluation
dict.keys() is already iterable, no need to convert to list

compliant.description: Preserves the lazy evaluation benefits of generators
Direct iteration over dict view objects

why_is_this_an_issue: Converting iterables to lists when only iteration is needed creates unnecessary memory allocation. This is particularly problematic with large datasets or generators that are designed for lazy evaluation. The list() constructor forces evaluation of the entire sequence into memory, which can cause performance degradation and memory exhaustion. Python's iteration protocol is designed to work efficiently with various iterable types without requiring conversion to lists.
how_to_fix: Remove the list() constructor call and iterate directly over the iterable object
If you need to modify the iterable during iteration, consider using a different approach like iterating over a copy or using list comprehensions
For generators and other lazy iterables, preserve their lazy nature by avoiding conversion to lists
Use appropriate data structures based on actual needs - lists only when random access or mutability is required
